sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Burton, Michigan?
sections.html:
A Burton homeowner can put the house on the market, sell it privately, or accept a cash purchase from a buyer who takes it with whatever work it needs. Each route ends with a deed recorded at the Genesee County Register of Deeds and transfer tax paid on the sale price.

Pick the route by looking at three things: how soon you must be out, what condition the house is in, and whether anything stands in the way of a clean title, such as back taxes, a lien or an unfinished estate. A listing rewards patience and a house that shows well. A cash sale rewards a seller who needs a firm date.

  • Agent listing: more buyers, but showings, appraisal and a buyer's lender add delay.
  • Private sale: no listing fee, with the paperwork on you.
  • Cash sale: fewer steps, and the buyer handles repairs after closing.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Burton for a home seller?
sections.html:
Burton is a suburb of Flint in Genesee County, and with about 29,300 residents it is the county's second largest city. It was Burton Township from 1856 and became a city in 1972 after residents voted to incorporate. The city covers roughly 23 square miles of land, which gives it more room between houses than the older, denser parts of Flint.

Two named neighborhoods show how the area is laid out. Belsay lies on Belsay Road at the rail line north of I-69 and Court Street, and Lapeer Heights sits at Belsay and Roberta Roads south of Lapeer Road. Buyers often search by those road names and by their distance to I-69.

One recent change matters for utility costs: Burton began receiving Karegnondi Water Authority water, treated by the Genesee County Drain Commission, in December 2017. A buyer comparing monthly costs may ask about water bills, so keep a recent statement handy.

sections.h2: Which Burton permit rules should you check before a sale?
sections.html:
Burton's Building Division publishes plain rules that decide whether past work will cause trouble with a buyer. The owner is responsible for making sure a permit was pulled, and unpermitted work can come up in an inspection or in the buyer's lender review.

  • A shed under 199 square feet needs a site permit; a structure of 200 square feet or more counts as a garage and needs a building permit.
  • Decks need permits unless they stand free at least 10 feet from the house and are under 200 square feet.
  • Finishing a basement requires a permit and an egress window.
  • In-ground pools need permits, and above-ground pools do when they stay up year round.
  • Cosmetic interior work such as paint and flooring needs no permit.

If you built a deck or finished the basement yourself, call the Building Division at 810-742-9230 and ask what is on file. Closing that gap before listing is cheaper than negotiating it afterward.

sections.h2: How do Burton property taxes work when a house sells?
sections.html:
Burton bills taxes twice a year and sets its own deadlines. Summer bills go out by July 1 and are due by September 30, and a one-time 4% penalty applies on October 1 with half a percent a month after that. Winter bills go out December 1 and are due by February 28. The city does not accept postmarks, so payment has to arrive at the Treasurer's office at 4303 S. Center Road by the due date.

On March 1 the account moves to the Genesee County Treasurer (810-257-3054), where a 4% collection fee and rising interest apply. The city states that property unpaid after two years is foreclosed and sold at auction.

Burton's page also explains Proposal A: taxable value is capped at the lesser of inflation or 5% a year while the owner stays, but it can rise to the state equalized value after a transfer. A buyer's first bill can therefore exceed yours. Principal residence exemption applications are due to the assessor by June 1, and you must file an update if your residence changes.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Genesee County cost?
sections.html:
The Genesee County Register of Deeds charges a $30 flat fee per document regardless of page count. Warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed containing a covenant of warranty need a $5 tax certification from the Genesee County Treasurer, paid by a separate check.

Transfer tax is listed at $7.50 per thousand for the state and $1.10 per thousand for the county, or $8.60 per thousand combined. The seller is liable, and the tax is calculated on the consideration paid. A $140,000 sale produces $1,204 of transfer tax. Michigan charges no transfer tax on mortgages.

Some transfers are exempt, including one from a parent to a child and a deed given to avoid foreclosure. The exemption must be written on the face of the deed.

sections.h2: When should a Burton seller consider a cash offer?
sections.html:
Consider it when the work a retail buyer would demand costs more than the discount a cash buyer applies. That often happens with houses needing a roof or mechanical work, estate properties with several heirs, and landlord-owned houses with unpaid rent.

Gather your tax bill, any permit records and a recent water statement, and ask each buyer for a written offer that spells out who pays closing costs. Compare at least two before you sign.

faqs.q: Does Burton require an inspection before I can sell my house?
faqs.a: Burton's published rules center on building permits and occupancy permits for work done on a property rather than a stated sale inspection. Call the Building Division at 810-742-9230 to confirm whether your address needs anything before closing.

faqs.q: How much will I pay in transfer tax selling a Burton house?
faqs.a: Genesee County lists the combined state and county rate at $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. A $120,000 sale would carry $1,032, and the seller is liable by statute unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: When are Burton summer and winter property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are due by September 30 and winter taxes by February 28, according to the city Treasurer. After March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Genesee County Treasurer with added fees and interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Burton house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. The owner is responsible for permits, and a buyer may ask for a discount or require the work to be legalized. A cash buyer usually accepts the condition and adjusts the price instead.

faqs.q: Do I lose my principal residence exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, the exemption stops when the house is no longer your principal residence. Michigan requires you to file a Request to Rescind (Form 2602) with the city assessor within 90 days, or a penalty of $5 a day up to $200 applies.
